title: Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
description:
Create fig_intercept_error in R using ggplot2 as a publication-ready scatter plot containing exactly three recorded results. Initialize the complete dataset explicitly as data.frame(b = c(0, 1.5, 3), mse = c(9, 2.25, 0)). Map numeric b to horizontal position and numeric mse to vertical position. Plot exactly (0, 9), (1.5, 2.25), and (3, 0). Do not add connecting lines, fitted curves, interpolation, uncertainty intervals, additional observations, observation-level data, or MAE values.

Render directly on a 9 × 6 inch landscape canvas. Export with ggsave(filename = 'fig_intercept_error.png', plot = fig_intercept_error, width = 9, height = 6, units = 'in', dpi = 300, bg = 'white'). Deliver this actual lossless PNG. Verify the exported file format and confirm dimensions of exactly 2700 × 1800 pixels, giving a 3:2 aspect ratio. Do not substitute a JPEG or obtain these dimensions by stretching, cropping, or resampling the supplied image. Inspect the final PNG for clipping, overlap, and adequate label spacing.

Use white plot and panel backgrounds and DejaVu Sans throughout. Set outer margins to 18 pt top, 24 pt right, 16 pt bottom, and 18 pt left. Use geom_point() with shape 21, size 4.2, stroke 0.6, fill #0072B2, outline #004A73, and full opacity. Draw markers above the grid. Marker appearance must not encode another variable.

Label the horizontal axis 'Added intercept correction b' and the vertical axis 'Mean squared error'. Keep both scales linear and continuous. Set horizontal breaks exactly at 0, 1.5, and 3, displayed as those strings. Set vertical breaks at 0, 2.25, 4.5, 6.75, and 9, without unnecessary trailing zeros. Use horizontal viewing limits of −0.35 to 3.35 and vertical viewing limits of −0.6 to 10.2, with no additional expansion. The space below zero provides marker clearance and does not represent negative MSE measurements.

Render axis titles at 13 pt, regular weight, in #222222, with 10 pt separation from tick labels. Render tick labels horizontally at 11 pt in #222222. Draw bottom and left axis lines in #6B7280 with 0.4 mm linewidth and outward ticks of 3 pt with 0.35 mm linewidth. Omit top and right borders. Show only horizontal major gridlines at the specified vertical ticks, using #E5E7EB and 0.3 mm linewidth. Omit vertical and minor gridlines.

Annotate the points with the exact strings '(0, 9)', '(1.5, 2.25)', and '(3, 0)'. Place their anchors at (0, 9.45), (1.5, 2.70), and (3, 0.45), respectively. Use horizontal centering and bottom alignment, equivalent to hjust = 0.5 and vjust = 0 in geom_text(). Use 12 pt regular text in #1F2937, converting point sizes to the geometry's native units as needed. Keep labels clearly separated from markers.

Render the title in exactly two lines: 'Recorded Mean Squared Error' followed by 'at Three Intercept Corrections'. Use 16 pt bold DejaVu Sans in #111827, align the title with the left edge of the plotting panel, and leave 12 pt below it. Do not display a legend.

Do not render a caption, footnote, or explanatory paragraph within the image. Keep this manuscript caption separate: 'Three recorded corrections evaluated on the same five synthetic observations used to determine the correction. No stochastic repetitions or held-out evaluation.' Communicate only the three recorded arithmetic results, without claims about unmeasured corrections or predictive generalization.
caption: Three recorded corrections evaluated on the same five synthetic observations used to determine the correction. No stochastic repetitions or held-out evaluation.

critic_history.suggestions: The three plotted pairs and axis ticks match the raw data: MSE is 9 at b = 0, 2.25 at b = 1.5, and 0 at b = 3. Equal horizontal spacing and the discrete presentation are appropriate. However, the title extends beyond the right edge and is truncated; wrap it across two lines while preserving every word. The explanatory caption is embedded in the image, violating the caption-exclusion requirement, and its first line is also clipped. Remove the caption from the image and retain it separately in the manuscript. All three coordinate labels touch or slightly overlap their markers; bottom-align the labels at their specified elevated anchors to create clear separation. The supplied image has a 4:3 aspect ratio rather than the requested 3:2 canvas; export at 9 × 6 inches and verify that all text and markers fit within the final bounds.

title: Residual Mean Correction and Same-Observation Evaluation
description:
Create a compact, publication-quality LaTeX/TikZ schematic on a pure white background, approximately 18 cm wide and 8 cm high, including the bottom routing channel and scope annotation. Preserve the original two-row, four-column arrangement, seven nodes, and all eight dependencies. Trim the large blank bands above and below the rendered content, leaving only a small, even outer margin. Modestly reduce the vertical separation between the upper and lower rows, particularly between the baseline and residual nodes, without crowding arrowheads or node outlines. Achieve the compact footprint through layout and cropping rather than shrinking the complete schematic. Use carefully aligned nodes and no figure title, caption text, or color legend.

Preserve the restrained, flat vector aesthetic: rounded rectangular nodes with 2 mm corner radii, uniform 0.7 pt outlines, and subtle pastel fills. Avoid shadows, gradients, textures, decorative icons, and three-dimensional effects. Set descriptive labels in a clean sans-serif font at 9–10 pt, with modest semibold emphasis for headings; use consistent LaTeX mathematical typography at 10–11 pt. Keep text near-black (#1F2937). Preserve these sizes at final manuscript scale. Use comfortable internal padding and clear separation between headings and equations. Measure the actual typeset width of every mathematical block, including continuation lines and superscripts, and keep all glyphs at least 2 mm inside their node borders. Adjust column widths and gaps to accommodate the text before finalizing the layout.

Retain the original palette as styling instructions only: input and target nodes use pale blue fill (#EAF3FB) and muted blue outlines (#829DB4); the fixed baseline uses pale blue-gray fill (#EEF2F6) and a slate-gray outline (#8795A5); observed residuals use pale amber fill (#FFF3DA) and a muted ochre outline (#B49B63); mean residual and corrected prediction use pale teal fill (#E7F3EF) and muted teal outlines (#6B9D92); evaluation uses very light lavender-gray fill (#F1EFF6) and a muted lavender-gray outline (#9892A5). Do not display a legend explaining these colors.

Arrange the elements as follows:

1. Upper left — supplied inputs. A pale blue node headed 'Input observations', containing \(\mathbf{x}=(-2,-1,0,1,2)\) on one mathematical line. Give the node sufficient width for the complete expression and its padding; do not isolate 'x=' above the vector.

2. Lower left — supplied targets. A matching pale blue node headed 'Observed targets', containing \(\mathbf{y}=2\mathbf{x}+3\cdot\mathbf{1}_5\), followed on a separate line by \(\mathbf{y}=(-1,1,3,5,7)\). Beneath these equations, include the compact definition \(\mathbf{1}_5=(1,1,1,1,1)\) at no less than 9 pt. Use an explicit centered multiplication dot between 3 and the bold ones vector so the expression cannot be mistaken for the number 31. Align the input and target nodes vertically and give them equal widths. Allow the target node sufficient height for its additional definition without compressing the equations.

3. Upper second column — baseline prediction. A pale blue-gray node headed 'Fixed baseline', containing the aligned calculation \(\widehat{\mathbf{y}}^{(0)}=2\mathbf{x}\), followed on the next line by \(=(-4,-2,0,2,4)\). Keep the equals signs aligned and make the numerical vector visibly part of the same calculation. Give this node enough width to contain the entire second line, including the horizontal space introduced by the alignment. The final 4 and closing parenthesis must remain fully inside the border with at least 2 mm clearance. Do not reduce the mathematical font size to fit the expression.

4. Lower second column — observed residuals. A pale amber node headed 'Observed residuals', containing \(\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{y}-2\mathbf{x}\), followed by \(\mathbf{r}=(3,3,3,3,3)\). Position it directly beneath the baseline node and horizontally beside the observed-target node. Match its width to the baseline node. Align the centers of the target, residual, mean-residual, and evaluation nodes so their lower-row dependencies remain straightforward.

5. Lower third column — scalar correction. A pale teal node headed 'Mean residual', containing the complete calculation \(b=\frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^{5}r_i=3\) on one display line. Keep 'b=' attached to the averaging expression. Make this node narrower than the vector-valued nodes only if the full equation and comfortable padding fit at the specified font size. Leave the upper third-column space open for the two dependencies entering the corrected prediction.

6. Upper right — corrected prediction. A pale teal node headed 'Corrected prediction', containing \(\widehat{\mathbf{y}}^{\,\mathrm{corr}}=2\mathbf{x}+b\cdot\mathbf{1}_5\), followed by \(\widehat{\mathbf{y}}^{\,\mathrm{corr}}=(-1,1,3,5,7)\). Use the same bold ones-vector notation defined in the target node and an explicit centered multiplication dot between b and that vector. Give the rightmost column sufficient width to accommodate both expressions without reducing mathematical type size.

7. Lower right — evaluation. A very light lavender-gray node headed 'Evaluate on the same five observations', wrapped across two balanced lines. Beneath the heading, display \(\mathbf{y}\quad\text{vs.}\quad\widehat{\mathbf{y}}^{\,\mathrm{corr}}\). Follow this with a two-line aligned equation: \(\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^{5}\left(y_i-\widehat y_i^{\,\mathrm{corr}}\right)^2\), then \(=0\), aligning the equals signs. Position this node directly beneath the corrected-prediction node and match their widths. Use deliberate line breaks and balanced internal spacing rather than compressed typography.

Draw every dependency explicitly using solid arrows approximately 0.9 pt thick, with consistent, compact, filled LaTeX-style arrowheads. Use dark slate (#334155) for supplied-value and baseline dependencies, and darker teal (#227C70) for the residual-to-mean and mean-to-correction dependencies. Keep arrow labels dark and legible, with a small white clearance around each label where necessary.

1. Draw a horizontal dark-slate arrow from the input node to the baseline node.

2. Draw a downward dark-slate arrow from the baseline node to the residual node. Shorten this connector through the reduced row spacing while maintaining clearly separate node boundaries and an unobstructed arrowhead.

3. Draw a horizontal dark-slate arrow from the observed-target node to the residual node.

4. Draw a darker teal horizontal arrow from the residual node to the mean-residual node. Place 'average residuals' on two balanced lines above the arrow. Reserve enough inter-node space for this label, with at least 1.5 mm clearance from the arrow and nearby node outlines. The mean-residual equation supplies the explicit count of five.

5. Draw a long horizontal dark-slate arrow from the baseline node to the corrected-prediction node through the open upper third-column space. Place the label \(2\mathbf{x}\) above the arrow.

6. Draw a separate darker teal arrow from the mean-residual node to the corrected-prediction node. Route it upward from the mean node through the open third-column space, then rightward into a lower port on the corrected node's left edge. Keep this horizontal segment visibly below the baseline arrow and label it \(b=3\). Use a clean orthogonal elbow with a subtly rounded corner. Do not intersect the baseline arrow or its label.

7. Draw a downward dark-slate arrow from the corrected-prediction node to the evaluation node.

8. Draw a separate dark-slate target-data arrow from the observed-target node to the evaluation node. Route it downward into a dedicated channel beneath the lower row, horizontally below all intervening nodes, then upward into the evaluation node's bottom edge. Label the horizontal segment 'observed targets: same five points'. Keep this channel close enough to the lower row to support the compact footprint, with clear separation from every node and from the annotation below.

Keep arrowheads immediately outside node borders, maintain consistent label offsets, and avoid arrow crossings or lines passing through nodes. Balance column spacing around both node contents and connector labels. Obtain the compact overall footprint by trimming outer whitespace, reducing excessive vertical gaps, and redistributing column widths without crowding the scalar correction or shrinking text.

Below the bottom routing channel and its label, retain one small, centered, visually subordinate note in dark gray at a readable final size of at least 9 pt: 'The correction is computed and evaluated on these same five observations.' Keep the gap between the routing label and this note modest but clearly legible. Leave only a small outer margin beneath the note. This is an explanatory scope annotation; keep the supplied figure caption separate from the image.

The finished schematic should communicate the exact finite calculation and its data dependencies. Scope the zero MSE explicitly to these five observations. Do not introduce held-out evaluation, predictive generalization, optimization, architecture, timing results, or additional experiments.
caption: Residual-mean correction for five synthetic observations with targets y = 2x + 3. The mean observed residual b = mean(y − 2x) = 3 is added to the fixed baseline prediction 2x. Evaluation on the same five observations used to compute the correction yields MSE = 0.

critic_history.suggestions: The diagram accurately matches the methodology and caption. All seven nodes and eight dependencies are present, and the arithmetic is correct: the baseline is (-4,-2,0,2,4), every residual is 3, their mean is b=3, and the corrected predictions equal the observed targets, giving MSE=0 on these same five observations. No unsupported experiments or generalization claims appear. Minor revisions would improve presentation: (1) The adjacent coefficient and bold ones vector in '3𝟭' can resemble the number 31; similarly, 'b𝟭' is insufficiently distinguished. Use explicit spacing and a defined five-dimensional ones vector, such as 3\,\mathbf{1}_5 and b\,\mathbf{1}_5, with its definition inside the target node. (2) The three-line 'average five residuals' connector label crowds the central gap. Shorten it to 'average residuals' on two lines, with clear separation from the arrow and adjacent boxes. The summation already specifies five residuals. (3) Trim the substantial blank upper margin and excess outer whitespace to approach the requested 18 cm by 8 cm footprint while preserving readable text. The figure contains neither the supplied caption nor a color legend; retain that separation. The bottom same-observation note is a useful scope annotation and should remain.
